structural_concerns: Customer concentration: the hyperscaler buyers (Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta) are estimated to be 40%+ of data-center revenue and are simultaneously NVDA's largest customers AND the funders of competing in-house silicon (TPU, Trainium, MTIA, Maia). A demand pause or accelerated ASIC migration by even one hits revenue cadence hard. Flagged by Damodaran, Burry, Munger.

Valuation leaves no margin of safety at a real cost of capital. Damodaran's base DCF ($132, beta 2.0/WACC 15.3%) and the 4-method valuation aggregate ($163) both sit 20-36% below the $205 price; residual income at the real cost of equity implies ~$68. Five of nine bull-lens personas went neutral purely on price. The downside on any multiple reset is large (Burry targets mid-$130s).
Inventory build: inventory rose 112% YoY to $21.4B (from $10.1B), outpacing even the revenue ramp. A demand softening would convert this to writedowns / margin pressure. Flagged by Burry.

InP (indium phosphide) optical-interconnect supply gating: China's export-licence regime on InP substrate (no substitute for high-speed optical scale-out; 6-inch wafer +250% to ~$5,000; AXT + Sumitomo ~80% of substrate, AXT producing most of its InP in China) is a real networking-ramp bottleneck for NVDA's optical/co-packaged-photonics roadmap. Mitigated: NVDA invested $2B each into Coherent and Lumentum in March to secure supply. Exposure MEDIUM, headwind not thesis-breaking.

Elevated volatility regime: 30-day annualized vol 43.7% vs 252-day 34.9% (expanding); 2-year max drawdown 36.9%. Beta 2.20 means the position carries roughly twice market risk and limited diversification benefit against an S&P-heavy book.

key_risks.title: Hyperscaler capex air-pocket
key_risks.description: AI infrastructure spend is concentrated in a handful of buyers; a 15-20%+ capex pullback in any single year would deflate the forward revenue path the valuation depends on and reset the multiple.

key_risks.title: Customer in-house silicon substitution
key_risks.description: The largest customers are funding custom ASICs that target inference share; faster-than-expected migration erodes NVDA's volume and pricing, especially as gross margins above 70% incentivize the switch.

key_risks.title: Valuation / multiple compression
key_risks.description: At a real (beta-2.0) cost of capital the base intrinsic value is ~$132, roughly 36% below price; the equity is priced for a near-flawless decade and any disappointment compresses the multiple sharply.

key_risks.title: AMD competitive share gain
key_risks.description: AMD's MI-series gaining double-digit training/inference share faster than modeled would pressure NVDA's volume growth and pricing power in the back half of the forecast window.

key_risks.title: InP optical-interconnect supply gating (regulatory)
key_risks.description: China's InP export controls throttle the optical substrate needed for AI scale-out networking (no near-term substitute, wafer prices +250%). Real near-term ramp risk for co-packaged optics, mitigated by NVDA's $2B stakes in Coherent and Lumentum and substitution over time.

key_risks.title: Inventory writedown risk
key_risks.description: Inventory +112% YoY to $21.4B ahead of the demand curve; a softening in orders converts the build into writedowns and a margin hit.

key_risks.title: Elevated volatility / drawdown
key_risks.description: Beta 2.20, 30d annualized vol ~44%, 2y max drawdown ~37%. High covariance with an already tech-heavy market limits diversification and forces a smaller prudent position size.

position_limit_reasoning: Volatility tier high (30d annualized vol 43.7%, in the 40-60% band): base max 3%. Adjustments: beta 2.20 and meaningful SPY correlation argue for limited diversification benefit (would deduct 1pp toward 2%), but the net-cash, no-leverage balance sheet removes any solvency-driven cut, and the 2y max drawdown of 37% is below the 50% penalty threshold. Net: hold at the 3% tier anchor. Final: 3.0%.
